trust_decision.summary: When a followed redirect is re-sent, the client decides whether the outgoing request keeps Expect/Cookie/Authorization/Proxy-Authorization by comparing the redirect target endpoint with the original endpoint; the fix adds 'secure target became insecure' so a protocol downgrade on the same host:port also strips them. Decided once, in the redirect send path.

landing_point.why: It is the only place in the main tree that removes the sensitive headers for a redirect (the four remove() calls at 620-631), so an engineer reading the summary 'leaks credentials on a protocol downgrade redirect' looks straight at this condition; the whole fix is one edit to this line.

fix_sites.entry_point: HttpClient.followRedirect(...) plus any request (e.g. HttpClient.get().uri(...).response()), inside HttpClientHandler.requestWithBody
fix_sites.module_kind: core client implementation (reactor-netty-http main, package-private handler reached from the public HttpClient API)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The Javadoc promises stripping only 'when redirecting to a different domain' (HttpClient.java:170, :926, :1018), so a same-host protocol downgrade and the websocket handshake path both read as outside the documented protection.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: An http->https upgrade redirect to the same host:port must keep Authorization/Cookie (the everyday 'redirect me to TLS' flow); because UriEndpoint.equals compares only the remote address, a fix keyed on 'the endpoint changed' or on 'the scheme changed' strips credentials there and breaks authenticated upgrade redirects. Same-host path-only redirects must likewise keep credentials.

O6_input_shapes: https://host:PORT -> http://host:PORT with an explicit non-default port (endpoints compare equal, so pre-fix nothing is stripped)
https://host -> http://host:443, where the redirect target names the secure port explicitly
wss://host:PORT -> ws://host:PORT (isSecure() covers wss/https only, see UriEndpoint.java:77-83)
downgrade occurring later in a multi-hop chain: fromURI is never updated by redirect(), so each hop is compared with the original request only (HttpClientConnect.java:672-695)
absolute Location vs relative Location resolved against the current URI (HttpClientConnect.java:679-684)
RedirectSendHandler sender (headers mutated in place, lines 619-624) vs the redirectRequestConsumer variant (lines 625-632)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A websocket request that follows a redirect never has the sensitive headers stripped: followRedirectPredicate is installed at line 586, then the websocket branch returns at 614 before the strip/redirectRequestConsumer wiring at 617-643, so defaultHeaders (Applied at 569-571) including Authorization/Cookie are re-sent to the redirect target, cross-host included. Redirects are raised for websockets at WebsocketClientOperations.java:148/:169 and Http2WebsocketClientOperations.java:111.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Websockets are a neighbouring feature with their own handshake send path; the advisory and all followRedirect Javadoc talk about HTTP redirects 'to a different domain', and the early return reads as deliberate, so a solver who only exercises a plain HTTP request never meets this route.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: guard bypass in the same file (lines 596-615); trigger 1-2 files away in the same package (WebsocketClientOperations.java:148, Http2WebsocketClientOperations.java:111)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Cookies carried by the request are re-added after the strip: beforeMarkSentHeaders runs the redirectRequestConsumer (which removes COOKIE) at 689-691 and then unconditionally rebuilds the COOKIE header from the request's cookie list at 698-700, so a cookie registered by the caller's doOnRequest/addCookie (HttpClientOperations.java:228-237, doOnRequest fires at REQUEST_PREPARED, HttpClientConfig.java:1205-1209) is sent to the redirect target even when it is another host.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: addCookie inside a redirect consumer is the documented way to deliberately re-add cookies on redirects (tested at HttpRedirectTest.java:773), and the advisory names credentials/Authorization, so the cookie list looks like intended caller-controlled behaviour.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one file away in the same package (HttpClientOperations.java:698-700 vs HttpClientConnect.java:618)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A websocket-only send path that enables redirect following but skips the sensitive-header strip.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The branch already exists and already installs followRedirectPredicate at line 586; a maintainer refining 'header handling during redirects' could plausibly have left the handshake path to its own logic.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Tracking the previous hop (updating fromURI inside redirect()) instead of comparing every hop with the original request.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: redirect() is where the redirect target replaces toURI, so a maintainer who wanted per-hop origin checks would naturally update fromURI there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Making the cookie-list re-add conditional on the redirect target matching the previous origin.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The redirect consumer and the cookie-list re-add sit three lines apart in the same method, so a maintainer fixing cookie leakage on redirect would edit exactly here.

O9_family: CWE-522 insufficiently protected credentials (sensitive request headers forwarded across a protocol-downgrade / cross-origin redirect)

O10_build.toolchain: Gradle 9.5.1 via the checked-in wrapper (gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties:3); multi-module build, project version 1.2.18-SNAPSHOT (gradle.properties:2); JDK required
O10_build.project_tests: reactor-netty-http/src/test/java/reactor/netty/http/client/HttpRedirectTest.java covers redirect handling (http->https at :478, relative redirect keeps scheme at :537, cookie re-add at :773) and HttpClientTest.java covers the client; all bind localhost-only servers. No test at the pinned commit asserts sensitive-header stripping on redirect, and the fix adds none.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Strip the sensitive headers whenever the endpoint or the scheme changed (compare toExternalForm/scheme instead of adding the secure->insecure case), which also strips on the everyday http->https upgrade redirect and breaks authenticated upgrade flows.

out_of_scope_notes: Nothing pursued outside this advisory. Noted without following: the transport-level proxy credentials in reactor-netty-core ProxyProvider.java:92-95 are a separate sink for PROXY_AUTHORIZATION.
